On which of the following intervals is the function $f(x)$ (shown above) invertible?

- $x\in (-3,0]$
- $x\in (-3,1)$
- $x\in [0,3)$
feedback.worked_solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test. 

- The given function is invertible on the intervals $x\in (-3,0]$ and $x\in [0,3).$ Indeed, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/00a80dde24ca012e0282362224c8b63764f5e149a8bfcda9c76ff4eb958fa93a.png)

 

- The given function is **not** invertible on the interval $x\in (-3,1)$  because some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/9ea54918e2ef4310b58e9cf8a0c9b1f9757a404d97dbbfd9e5b037af2193f38c.png)

 

Hence, the correct answer is 'I and III only''.
